title: The projective line is a genus-zero smooth proper connected curve
statement: Let $k$ be an algebraically closed field and let $P=\mathbf P^1_k=\mathbf P(\{0,1\};\operatorname{Spec}k)$ [def-nagata-projective-space-base-change]. Then $P$ is a smooth proper connected curve over $k$ [def-sc-curves] and its genus [def-sc-genus] is zero: $H^1(P,\mathcal O_P)=0$.

source.place: Tag 0B2P, varieties.tex, lemma-projective-space-smooth (n=1: smooth projective variety of dimension one); Tag 0C6U, curves.tex, proposition-projective-line, implication (1) to (2) and (7); properness of projective space is the existing lemma-nagata-projective-space-base-change-proper

proof.text: Construct the two charts of the base-change model explicitly. In the degree-zero localization of $\mathbf Z[x_0,x_1]$ at $x_0$, a homogeneous degree-zero fraction $F/x_0^m$, with $F=\sum_{j=0}^m a_jx_0^{m-j}x_1^j$, maps to $\sum_{j=0}^m a_jt^j$, where $t=x_1/x_0$. Its inverse sends $t^j$ to $x_1^j/x_0^j$; multiplying numerator and denominator by $x_0$ leaves the image unchanged, and monomial independence proves injectivity. Thus this ring is $\mathbf Z[t]$. On the other chart $F/x_1^m$, with $F=\sum_{j=0}^m b_jx_1^{m-j}x_0^j$, maps to $\sum_{j=0}^m b_js^j$, with inverse $s^j\mapsto x_0^j/x_1^j$, so its ring is $\mathbf Z[s]$. The basic opens cover by [def-nagata-affine-proj] since $x_0,x_1$ generate the irrelevant ideal. Base change to $k$ using [lem-weil-pbc-fibre-product-affine-spectra] gives $k\otimes_{\mathbf Z}\mathbf Z[t]\cong k[t]$ (send $a\otimes t^j$ to $at^j$, with inverse $\sum a_jt^j\mapsto\sum a_j\otimes t^j$), and $k\otimes_{\mathbf Z}\mathbf Z[s]\cong k[s]$ by $a\otimes s^j\mapsto as^j$ with inverse $\sum a_js^j\mapsto\sum a_j\otimes s^j$. The preimages of the two basic opens cover the fibre product, since each point projects into one of them. In the first chart the overlap inverts $t=x_1/x_0$, and in the second it inverts $s=x_0/x_1$, so its rings are identified by $s=t^{-1}$. This is exactly the gluing presentation of the polynomial Proj and standard cover of [def-sc-p1-standard], so the chart identifications glue, with identical transition $s=t^{-1}$, to an isomorphism over $k$ with that model.

source.place: Tag 0B2P, lemma-projective-space-smooth: supply its omitted chart argument

proof.text: Each of these two charts is $\mathbf A^1_k$, so [sbc-lem-affine-space-smooth] gives smoothness of relative dimension one on both. The affine-local description in [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms] checks smoothness on these covering charts; the relative fibre dimension condition is local at each point and equals one on its chart. Thus $P\to\operatorname{Spec}k$ is smooth of relative dimension one.

The polynomial rings $k[t]$ and $k[s]$ are domains: the product of two nonzero polynomials has nonzero leading coefficient. In each spectrum the prime $(0)$ has closure $V(0)$ equal to the whole spectrum; hence every two nonempty opens meet, and each chart is irreducible, in particular connected. The intersection is nonempty, for evaluation $t\mapsto1$ defines a point of $\operatorname{Spec}k[t,t^{-1}]$. If $P$ were the union of disjoint nonempty open-and-closed pieces, each connected chart would lie entirely in one piece, and their common point would force both charts into the same piece, a contradiction. Thus $P$ is nonempty and connected. Apply [lem-sbc-smooth-fixed-dimension-over-field] with $n=1$ and step 2 to obtain $\dim P=1$.

Apply [lemma-nagata-projective-space-base-change-proper] to the finite homogeneous-coordinate set $\{0,1\}$ and base $\operatorname{Spec}k$: $P\to\operatorname{Spec}k$ is proper. Properness includes separatedness and finite type by [def-weil-proper-morphism]. With smoothness from step 2 and nonempty connected dimension one from step 3, these are all clauses in the connected-curve convention of [def-sc-curves].

source.place: Projective-line properness and the curve convention

proof.text: Under the explicit standard-chart identification of step 1, use [lem-sc-p1-monomial](ii) with $d=0\geq-1$ to obtain $H^1(P,\mathcal O(0))=0$. The gluing rule of [def-sc-p1-standard] for $d=0$ is $g_0=g_1$; sending $g_i$ to $1$ identifies $\mathcal O(0)$ with $\mathcal O_P$, with equal maps on the overlap. Thus $H^1(P,\mathcal O_P)=0$. The genus definition [def-sc-genus], applicable by step 4 and algebraic closedness of $k$, now gives $g(P)=\dim_k0=0$.
